newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS seen raising cargo rates soon - sources.
newsitem.headline: SAS seen raising cargo rates soon - sources.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS is expected to raise its cargo rates soon, industry sources said.
"We are expecting rate increases. They haven't told us yet but we believe so," one freight forwarder told Reuters.
"We have just been notified from the Far East to Europe that rates are increasing. It seems like everyone is trying to go for 10 percent," said the forwarder, who asked to be unnamed.
No one at SAS would comment on the report.
Lufthansa Cargo AG said earlier on Thursday it would meet next week to consider air cargo rate increases from the Scandinavian market and hinted that the market was busy enough to support a rise.
Peer Skriver Hansen, manager for Swissair cargo, said the airline was considering rate increases and was waiting for a cue from other airlines, especially KLM and Lufthansa.
"We will look into what the market does and will look into getting something between three and five percent. We're still in the investigation stage," Hansen told Reuters.
"KLM and Lufthansa are the market leaders, at least on the European scale. The rest of us will try to follow suit," Hansen added.
